description: At approximately 9:20 am on 6/21/23, Perdido experienced a Platform shut down due to a VFD failure. The "variable frequency device" is the controller for the caisson ESPs located in the platform's subsea MMC control room. The smoke detectors in the subsea control building were automatically activated by the smoke that was released from the VFD cabinet. This initiated a PSD - Platform Shut Down. A full muster was accounted for in 7 minutes. No escalation outside of the subsea MMC control room. The ICS team dispatched the fire team to a staging area and then to the Sub-Sea MCC. The fire team only observed smoke (no fire) from the VFD failure. Once the area was secured, an electrician was then dispatched to the building to begin surveying the cabinets. No notable temperature differences noted on the outside of the cabinets. Permission was given to open the cabinet on A and a temperature in excess of 350F was observed. Continued survey of the B, C, and D cabinets and ~210F temperature was observed. At that point, the team felt they had identified and isolated the source of the smoke which was detected. A fire watch was staged and the fire team to report back to debunker. The community was allowed to leave muster but not allowed to return to work. Recovery: The building was ventilated, smoke cleared, and AHU's returned to service. Once all smoke detectors were clear, the doors were closed to the building and smoke detection was continuously monitored. A LOTO was installed on the struck by breakers for ESP-A VFD. The team then proceeded to apply power to the other available ESP VFD's in the building to verify their health (B, C, D). All appeared to have no issues. General community was then allowed to return to work. After speaking with Marco DeLeon w/BSEE and getting a verbal approval to start, the crew proceeded to run ESP - B to secure part of the sub-sea system for flow assurance (hydrate prevention). The team then moved on to ESP-D followed by ESP-C, ensuring their health. Once B-caisson wells were deemed safe they were started on initial ramps. The employee had been using unspecified personal prot ective equipment.

description: On 06/22/24 at approximately 13:23, the HP Oil Separator (MBD-115) level safety LT-115A was to be tested for the high/low shutdown. The HP oil separator was not in use at the time. An ACR, who has performed this task many times in the past, identified that there was sufficient level in the vessel based on the LT-115A level measurement. They started the testing process by closing the upper vessel isolation valves and opening the needle valve on top of the level bridle. The ball valve that allows gas to flow (bleed) to the skid was slightly opened to allow gas pressure to pressurized line and the level to rise in the bridle by reducing the pressure above the liquid level. The indicated level in the bridle rose faster than expected and the ACR closed the ball valve. The control room operator (CRO) radioed that the high-level shutdown setpoint was not reached and the ACR re-opened the ball valve allowing gas to flow to the skid and allowing the level to rise. Again, the bridle level rose quickly and reached the LSH setpoint. The ACR then proceeded to prepare the draining of the liquids by closing the lower vessel isolation valve and opening the upper vessel isolation valve. Before draining the liquids the ASH-1017 and ASH-1008 detected sufficient gas (2oo45) with 1017 being in "Alarm" (25% LEL) and 1008 at least in "warning" (10% LEL) . This resulted in a platform shutdown (PSD) per the Cause and Effects. The technician performing the check notified the CCR immediately. Note: Gas detectors that came into alarm that then caused shut down, cleared instantly. 11 wells were flowing (in service) during the time of event. No muster was involved because it was known what caused the incident and it was not an ICS event. The cause was due to the Technician bleeding a level bridal too fast causing the volume of gas to make its way to 2 Gas detectors. Since this was a human performance event, coaching was conducted with the individual. There were no damages to the equipment, no injuries, and no hot work being performed.
